findings.description: Homepage copy says 'about 5 years now, two of them in DevOps and the rest in full-stack development'. /whoami, person.ts and llms.txt all state DevOps Jan 2022 - Mar 2026 (about 4y2m) and full-stack from Apr 2026 (about 4 months). findings.title: /logs description is 66 chars of Vercel starter boilerplate
findings.description: 'Insights, experiments, and stories to follow along with my journey' in src/seo/copy.ts:12-14 names no entity and no topic. It also supplies the Blog JSON-LD description and the channel description of all three feeds, so one weak string reaches four surfaces. Every post description on the site is better written than the hub page's.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite at 140-160 chars in copy.ts, e.g. 'Field logs from Sandev Abeykoon - first-hand write-ups on cloud infrastructure, DevOps, distributed systems and the projects that broke along the way.'

findings.title: Seven posts have zero contextual internal links in either direction
findings.description: Excluding site nav, the archive forms two clusters - infrastructure (ansible-cloud-config, aws-cloud, cloud-backup-pipeline, monitoring-system, building-on-premise-server, backup-cli, building-chamilion-2025) and applications (distributed-architecture, jwt-microservice-auth, local-first-pwa, hive-bug-tracker) - joined by a single link. Outside both: wordpress-survival-guide, cost-to-make-a-website, dsa-notes, game-design, init, work-and-contribution, a41sl-bot.
findings.recommendation: Add 2-3 in-prose contextual links per isolated post in both directions, matching the existing house style. wordpress-survival-guide is the highest priority - it is the most link-worthy asset on the site and has no internal links pointing at it.

findings.title: Three posts skip heading levels
findings.description: building-on-premise-server (h1 -> h3 'Hardware'), wordpress-survival-guide (h1 -> h3 '1. Network Hardening'), distributed-architecture (h2 'Implementation Patterns' -> h4). Headings are what get extracted as standalone passages for AI answers, so a broken ladder weakens retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Mechanical heading-level shifts in the MDX source.

findings.title: Four posts have no subheadings at all
findings.description: backup-cli, hive-bug-tracker and work-and-contribution render as a bare h1 plus an unbroken block; a41sl-bot has a single h2. No structure means no extractable passages and no anchor targets.
findings.recommendation: Add h2s to break the existing prose into sections - no new copy required.

findings.title: No title template, so post titles carry no brand
findings.description: Root layout.tsx has no title.template. A SERP entry reads 'Backup CLI: MySQL and Filesystem Backups over SFTP in Rust' with nothing tying it to the site or author.
findings.recommendation: Optional. Most metaTitle values are already 52-60 chars and a suffix would truncate - shorten them first or skip.

findings.title: Three animated GIFs total 6.0 MB and were served unoptimized
findings.description: next/image passed animated GIFs through untouched - the /_next/image?...&w=828&q=75 URL returned the full 2 678 977 B original at audit time. That GIF was the mobile LCP element at 1452 ms unthrottled (2026-08-11 measurement); on a real 4G link 2.68 MB alone was roughly 13 s of transfer. Independent of the CLS/lazy-load fix - same root files, different problem.
findings.recommendation: Done: all three re-encoded to animated WebP with sharp({ animated: true }). godzilla-dance 2 678 977 B -> 194 902 B (-92.7%), dark-souls 1 285 453 B -> 186 610 B (-85.5%), family-guy-car-crash (58 frames at 360x360, more motion data per pixel, needed quality 60 vs 75 for the other two) 2 040 477 B -> 775 236 B (-62.0%). Total 6 004 907 B -> 1 156 748 B (-80.7%). .gif sources deleted, MDX imports updated, unoptimized kept on each PostImage (animated WebP gets the same next/image pass-through treatment GIF did). Verified via npm run build + served HTML: /_next/static/media/*.webp with real dimensions, no /_next/image proxy hop.

LLM answers preferentially cite entities corroborated across independent sources.

findings.title: Fallback src requests the 3840px variant
findings.status: still open, 2026-08-14 - original prediction was wrong
findings.description: Every image's bare src attribute is still ...&w=3840&q=75, live-verified 2026-08-14. The original finding predicted this would resolve once real dimensions were passed - it did not: next/image sets the bare src to its largest configured breakpoint by design, independent of intrinsic dimensions. Still low real-world impact since modern browsers use srcset and ignore it.
findings.recommendation: No fix currently planned; low priority given browsers ignore the bare src in practice. Note for future audits: do not assume this resolves itself alongside the dimension fix.
